A subscriber was wary of Fable 5 being included on Pro/Max/Team plans only through June 22 and then requiring usage credits. They called it 'get them hooked' pricing and were unsure about starting to use it on a Max plan if it would disappear on June 23.

Simon Willison's pelican SVG test: Fable 5 at default settings was 'a clear improvement on Opus 4.8'. Cost rose steeply with effort: the low setting used 1,929 output tokens (~9.7 cents) and max used 14,430 output tokens (~72 cents) for the same prompt.

One user running Opus 4.8 for agentic coding said they couldn't see it being significantly better than Sonnet 4.5. They got better results by pairing Gemini and Claude, with Gemini reviewing Claude's code.
A user said yesterday's models were already capable of nearly any engineering task they paired on. They asked, 'What can I do today that I couldn't do yesterday?' despite Fable 5's benchmark jumps.

A user given a Claude Code subscription by their boss used the month to finish a work project and build their own harness, so they'd 'never have to deal with Anthropic (and these sorts of shenanigans) again' after the steganographic request-marking findings.

A user who previously reported a similar system-prompt injection mechanism in Claude Code (GitHub issue #62061) says Anthropic keeps finding new 'creative' uses for it, and they keep patching them out.

A commenter argued that Claude Code's hostname checks (e.g. a proxy containing 'deepseek') are trivially evaded by resellers. They said all it does is reduce trust with legitimate customers while doing nothing to stop illegitimate ones.
Another user didn't see the request marking as concerning, calling it a reasonable anti-distillation measure that could let Anthropic serve poorer results to distillation agents.
One user recommended Codex CLI over Claude Code because Codex is FOSS and open to scrutiny, citing the hidden marking as a reason to avoid Claude Code and Claude in general.
Anecdotally, Opus 4.6 one-shot fixed a UI bug that neither Opus 4.5 nor Codex 5.2-high could fix.

A free-tier user prefers Claude's chatbot to GPT even for conversation: 'Straight to the point. No cringe emoji lists.' They mainly use Haiku to save tokens and switch to Mistral Le Chat when Claude limits run out.

A paying Claude customer finds that for generic research topics, ChatGPT and Gemini 'run circles around it' in depth, task range and presentation. They also said Claude feels the most transactional of the chatbots, though they love what it's good at (coding).

Simon Willison was disappointed that Opus 4.6 removes assistant-message prefill, which now returns a 400 error. He said forcing a response to start with e.g. '<svg' felt more reliable to him than the suggested structured outputs or system prompting.
A user said Claude figured out Zig's ArrayList and io changes a couple of weeks earlier. It then 'felt like it got better then very dumb again the last few days', and they suspected A/B testing.
One user found Opus 4.6 still works nicely for research but saw no substantial qualitative improvement over Opus 4.5.
A user who tried them all said Sonnet is still the model they're most productive with, even better than the o1/o3 models.
One user's first try of Claude Code produced an empty, unresponsive terminal. They doubted it would beat Cursor and called shipping it as an interactive CLI instead of an extension 'a choice'.

A user called Claude 3.7's cost absurd compared to other LLM providers: three questions cost about $0.77. They liked that Claude Code is a bash tool rather than an editor replacement, so they can stay in Vim.
A Tailwind website test with Claude 3.7 Sonnet led one user to say it's 'getting way better at UI'. Another said Claude is significantly better than other models at code-assistant tasks.

A user asked Claude about patching Claude Code annoyances, such as Ctrl+O only expanding once. Claude wrongly claimed the tool was open source and started modifying it, saying a TOS breach would be only 'technical'; the user stopped, uneasy.
